title: Introduce concurrency budget regulator and adaptive slot throttle for dedicated fleets
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: dedicated fleets were showing tail-latency spikes and unfair slot consumption during transient surges where a small subset of tenants consumed disproportionate concurrency slots. This PR introduces a concurrency budget regulator and an adaptive slot throttle that together limit per-lease concurrency spend, smooth transient bursts, and give the autoscaler better headroom signals. Approach: 1) add a lightweight budget ledger that tracks per-lease concurrency consumption over a sliding window (configurable window and decay), 2) introduce an adaptive slot throttle that reduces new concurrency grants when a lease exceeds its budget percentile using a proportional backoff curve, 3) expose lease-level budget_utilization and throttle_factor metrics to allow informed autoscaler and operator decisions, 4) add feature-flag gating and a canary rollout path with rollout policies to enable gradual ramp to dedicated fleets. Compatibility and rollout: behavior is gated behind the feature flag "concurrency-budget" defaulting to off; when enabled the regulator only intervenes after a short warmup to avoid disturbing steady-state reservations. Safety: built-in bypass for SLA-backed reservation contracts and a fast-path for internal system tenants. Tests and observability: unit tests for ledger accounting, property tests for the throttle curve, end-to-end bench harness for mixed-tenant synthetic load, and Grafana dashboard JSON for new metrics. Impact: reduces observed 99.9th latency by up to 38% in our internal bench and lowers tail token-cost in contended clusters. See linked Linear tickets for rollout checklist.
